Ally Bank's second annual fandom survey finds Gen Z overtaking millennials as the highest-spending generation and helping fuel a 40% year-over-year jump in women's sports spending.

CHARLOTTE, N.C., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ally Bank's second annual Cost of Fandom report findings paint a picture of a generation caught between passion and preparation. Gen Z sports fans now spend more on fandom than any other generation — an average of $2,000 a year — while also reporting greater financial tradeoffs such as cutting back on essentials (59%), delaying savings (55%) and taking on extra work (56%). 

Gen Z is also leading the shift toward women's sports, dedicating 34% of their sports spending to the category. That reflects a broader trend among all sports fans: annual spending on women's sports rose 40% to $700, while men's sports spending held steady at $950, signaling the growing commercial potential of women's sports.

"Fans have always known the value of women's sports. Now the business world is catching up," said Andrea Brimmer, chief marketing and public relations officer at Ally. "Younger fans in particular are turning passion into real momentum for the game. Every ticket purchased, game watched and team supported is an investment in the future of women's sports. At Ally, we believe fans deserve more opportunities to experience the moments that make it all worth it."

Intent is there, but follow-through lags. More than one-third (35%) would consider saving specifically for sports, yet only 15% have dedicated savings, essentially unchanged from last year.

"Today's fans are thinking more about where their money goes, but that awareness hasn't fully translated into action," said Jack Howard, head of money wellness at Ally. "The goal isn't spending less on what you love but making a plan that lets you enjoy it. Setting aside a little 'fandom fund' for the experiences you love can help make them part of your financial plan without losing sight of your bigger goals."

The numbers reveal what fandom costs. The choices fans make reveal what it's worth. Read the full 2026 Cost of Fandom Report HERE.

Fandom Isn't Getting Benched, Even When It Means Making Tough Calls

  • Sports spending holds steady. Fans spend about $1,600 a year on fandom, unchanged from 2025. More than half (52%) say spending stayed the same, while more increased spending (27%) than cut back (18%).
  • Gen Z takes the spending lead. About one in three Gen Z (33%) and millennial (32%) fans report spending more, versus 12% of boomers.
  • For many, fandom is worth the money. More than one-third of women's sports fans (36%) and men's sports fans (39%) give their fandom high marks for being worth the cost, while just 7% of either group give it low marks.

A More Mindful Spending Playbook Is Taking Shape

  • More fans are setting boundaries. Nearly three in 10 (28%) set strict spending limits, up four percentage points from 2025, while fewer give sports spending little thought (13% vs. 18%).
  • Women's sports fans have an edge in the savings game. One in five (20%) have dedicated sports savings, while 42% would consider setting money aside, compared with 35% of fans overall.

Fans Are Fueling the Next Chapter for Women's Sports

  • Women's sports fans have increased spending. More than one-third of women's sports fans (36%) report spending more over the past year, nearly double the share who spent less (19%).
  • A new generation is reshaping women's sports fandom. Nearly three-quarters (74%) of Gen Z women's sports fans became fans in the past decade, compared with 49% of women's sports fans overall and 23% of men's sports fans. Gen Z also dedicates a larger share of its sports spending to women's sports (34%) than millennials (29%) or boomers (13%), signaling significant long-term commercial potential.
  • Women's basketball wins with younger fans. More than one-third of Gen Z sports fans (35%) identify as big or fanatical women's basketball fans, compared with 27% of millennials, placing the sport among the top five for both generations.
  • Men are helping fuel the momentum. Women make up the majority of women's sports fans (62%), but men are more likely to report increased spending on women's sports (43% vs. 32%).
  • Fan loyalty extends beyond the game. Almost one in four women's sports fans (22%) have chosen a brand because of its support for women's sports, highlighting the influence of fandom on purchasing decisions.
  • Access has its challenges, but fans are finding ways to connect. Women's sports fans who report having more difficulty participating in the fandom cite ticket prices (38%), travel expenses (31%), venue accessibility (24%) and TV or streaming access (21%) as barriers. Meanwhile, nearly one-third (31%) of women's sports fans have paid for streaming specifically to watch women's sports.
  • Support for women's sports goes beyond fandom. Nearly half of women's sports fans (49%) agree that supporting women's sports contributes to gender equality and empowerment, reflecting the values that help shape their connection to the game.

Making Room for What Matters
Fans show up for more than the game itself. They show up for the moments that become memories, the communities they find and the teams they believe in. Those experiences carry a value that goes far beyond the final score, reminding us why fandom is worth investing in.

Through Money Roots®, Ally's free financial wellness program, consumers can explore how their money mindset influences the way they spend, save and invest. For more information, visit ally.com/moneyroots.

Survey Methodology: In September 2026, Ally surveyed 2,100 sports fans across Gen Z, millennial, Gen X and Boomer populations to better understand financial behaviors and consequences of fandom.

CGMI and CGBI are designed to bring income to the core of client portfolios

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Capital Group, one of the world's largest and most experienced active investment managers, today announced the listing of two new active multi-asset exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Capital Group Multi-Asset Income ETF (CGMI) and Capital Group Multi-Asset Income Builder ETF (CGBI) began trading today on the New York Stock Exchange, expanding Capital Group's active multi-asset ETF suite to three strategies alongside Capital Group Core Balanced ETF (CGBL). Capital Group now has a suite of 27 active ETFs in the U.S. and is one of the largest active ETF issuers, with more than $160 billion in AUM.1 The launch builds on the success of the Capital Group Core Balanced ETF (CGBL), which was introduced three years ago, has grown to $7.9 billion in AUM, and is the largest multi-asset ETF in the U.S. market.2

The two new ETFs are:

  • Capital Group Multi-Asset Income ETF (CGMI)  
    CGMI seeks to provide current income through a multi-asset approach. Its focus on dividend-paying equities and bonds can also help provide a measure of downside protection. 
  • Capital Group Multi-Asset Income Builder ETF (CGBI) 
    CGBI seeks to combine the potential for current and rising income and help dampen volatility. Global exposure plays an active role in this fund and its ability to grow income over time.

"We've consistently heard from advisors that they are looking for more ways to incorporate income into client portfolios," said Scott Davis, Head of ETFs at Capital Group. "To meet these needs, we have drawn inspiration from the growth of our first multi-asset ETF, CGBL, and designed two additional active multi-asset strategies. CGMI and CGBI build on Capital Group's long history of combining equities and fixed income to create income-generating portfolios, delivering those capabilities through the efficiency and flexibility of the ETF wrapper."

TFIX is a multisector fixed income solution seeking to maximize total return through income and capital appreciation across multiple credit sectors. Following a similar investment framework to that of the Capital Appreciation Fund's fixed income portfolio, the ETF intends to invest in areas of the fixed income market that have historically offered the highest risk adjust returns – including intermediate maturity Treasuries, BBB-rated investment grade debt, high yield bonds, and floating rate leveraged loans. CANNES, France, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --

The program features a live Eco Wave Power demonstration of trusted energy transactions for AI data centers, a Quobly silicon quantum computing exhibit, and sessions on post-quantum cybersecurity, optical networking and secure satellite communications.

SEALSQ Corp (NASDAQ: LAES) ("SEALSQ" or "Company"), a company that focuses on developing and selling Semiconductors, PKI, and Post-Quantum technology hardware and software products, today announced that it is showcasing its Quantum Sovereign Vertical Stack at the SEALSQ Quantum Days, now underway at the Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic in Cannes. Following the inaugural World Quantum Cannes Festival, the event brings together SEALSQ’s international teams, technology partners and industry experts to demonstrate practical cybersecurity applications and discuss the infrastructure needed for a future quantum internet.

In his opening keynote, From Quantum Capabilities to Quantum Systems, SEALSQ’s Founder and CEO, Carlos Moreira presented the Group’s “Root-to-Qubit-to-Space” architecture. Developed through the SEALQuantum initiative, it starts with a hardware root of trust to authenticate devices, extends that trust to the electronics and networks that operate quantum computers, and applies the same principles to satellites and ground infrastructure. The objective is to help governments and enterprises retain control over critical technologies, cryptographic keys and sensitive data.

“Cannes is where the quantum industry is moving from promise to products,” said Mr. Moreira. “Quantum computing will change how we compute, and it will also break the cryptography that protects today’s infrastructure. Trust has to be issued in hardware. With Quantum Days, we bring together the people building quantum systems and the people securing them, so that both move forward together.”

Root - Post-quantum cybersecurity and trusted energy transactions
SEALSQ is highlighting how its QS7001 post-quantum secure element, hardware roots of trust and public key infrastructure (PKI) can help organizations migrate existing systems to quantum-resistant cryptography. The program covers practical applications in access control, enterprise cybersecurity, energy infrastructure, automotive systems, medical devices and biometric authentication.

In a live demonstration, Inna Braverman, Founder and CEO of Eco Wave Power, and Jonathan Llamas, Chief Product & Strategy Officer of SEALCOIN, joined Mr. Moreira to present progress under the three-year memorandum of understanding between SEALSQ, its parent company WISeQey Corp. ( “WISeQey”) (Nasdaq/SIX: WQEY), a global quantum cybersecurity and space IoT company, its sister company SEALCOIN which develops decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) technology and the SEALCOIN platform, and Eco Wave Power. The demonstration showed how authenticated data from wave-energy infrastructure can support auditable machine-to-machine energy transactions for AI data centers. The collaboration combines Eco Wave Power’s renewable-energy infrastructure with SEALSQ’s hardware security, WISeQey’s digital identity and PKI, and SEALCOIN’s transaction technology. The partners plan to explore integrating the QS7001 to strengthen the long-term security of connected energy infrastructure.

On October 27, SEALSQ announced that QS7001 V1 passed all physical and functional security tests in its Common Criteria EAL5+ technical evaluation at SERMA. The milestone also benefits VaultIC409 and QVault TPM, which share the same hardware platform and were scheduled for display at electronica 2026 in Munich the week before Cannes. As of September 30, 2026, 42 prospective customers and partners were evaluating QS7001 and QVault TPM.

“Our customers are not asking whether to migrate to post-quantum security, they are asking how and when,” said Loïc Hamon, Chief Operating Officer of SEALSQ. “Quantum Days is built around their questions: certified chips, PKI migration, custom ASICs and the real-life experience of companies that have already started.”

Qubit — Building security into quantum computing hardware
A Quobly silicon quantum computing system is on display in Cannes. SEALSQ led Quobly’s €115 million Series A, followed by a $5 million commercial agreement to integrate cryogenic CMOS intellectual property and post-quantum security into platforms built around Quobly’s silicon spin qubits. The work addresses practical security needs such as authenticating control electronics, securely provisioning devices and protecting communications between quantum processors and the classical systems that operate them. SEALSQ has also invested in EeroQ, a Chicago-based company developing an electron-on-helium quantum computing architecture.

SEALSQ is also highlighting its November 18 announcement that it signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Australia-based QuintessenceLabs. The proposed acquisition would combine SEALSQ’s secure semiconductors and PKI with QuintessenceLabs’ quantum random number generation and enterprise cryptographic key and policy management capabilities.

Space - Connecting quantum processors, optical networks and satellites
Through SEALQuantum, SEALSQ acquired Miraex and its quantum photonic interconnect technology. Miraex’s thin-film lithium tantalate platform is designed to bridge the microwave frequencies used by certain quantum processors and the optical frequencies used in communications networks. Such interfaces could enable quantum processors to exchange quantum information over optical links, a capability needed for a future quantum internet.

The space program examines how post-quantum chips can be integrated into payloads for the WISeSat.Space constellation. Near-term applications include authenticating satellites and ground terminals and protecting command links with post-quantum cryptography. Longer-term work explores how optical and quantum communications could connect terrestrial and orbital networks. WISeSat.Space Holdings (Nasdaq: SAIQ) is a SEALSQ sister company.

Today’s program highlights

  • From Quantum Capabilities to Quantum Systems -Opening keynote by Carlos Moreira.
  • Quantum Computing That Works: From Hardware to Hybrid Systems - Panel with QuantA, Quobly and Daniel Brau, Chief Quantum Officer of SEALSQ.
  • Post-Quantum Cryptography: Revolution or Simple Evolution? - Keynote by Pierre-Yvan Liardet, Chief Scientist at eShard.
  • Challenges and Opportunities on the Migration Path towards Post-Quantum Security - Practical feedback from LEGIC, Eviden, Hitachi Energy and Precise Biometrics.
  • Cybersecurity in the AI and Quantum Era - Keynote by Loïc Hamon, Chief Operating Officer of SEALSQ.
  • Powered by LEGIC and Secured by SEALSQ - Talk by Mehdi Elhaoussine, General Manager of LEGIC.
  • Trusted Energy Transactions for AI Data Centers - Live demonstration and discussion with Eco Wave Power and SEALCOIN.
  • Vision and Strategy for a Quantum-Safe PKI Migration - Panel with Hitachi Cyber and WISeQey Trust Services. WISeQey Corp (Nasdaq: WQEY) is SEALSQ’s parent company.
  • QASIC: Quantum-Resistant ASIC Design for Automotive and Medical Applications - Keynote by David Fresneau, Strategic Marketing Director of IC’Alps, SEALSQ’s ASIC design subsidiary.
  • Engineering the Quantum Edge in Orbit - Panel on post-quantum chips and payload integration for the WISeSat.Space constellation.
  • Closing fireside chat - Carlos Moreira in conversation with Nick Farina, CEO of EeroQ.

About SEALSQ:
SEALSQ is a leading innovator in Post-Quantum Technology hardware and software solutions. Our technology seamlessly integrates Semiconductors, PKI (Public Key Infrastructure), and Provisioning Services, with a strategic emphasis on developing state-of-the-art Quantum Resistant Cryptography and Semiconductors designed to address the urgent security challenges posed by quantum computing. As quantum computers advance, traditional cryptographic methods like RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) are increasingly vulnerable.

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Prefeasibility Study outcome: after tax NPV of approximately US$1.3B at an 8% real discount rate and after-tax IRR of 24% for Cowboy State Mine, with pre-production capital of US$840M including contingency
  • Value upside under way: recovery optimisation with Novex has commenced, and each one percentage point increase in NdPr recovery adds approximately US$50 million to NPV⁸
  • Greater definition and confidence: capital and operating costs estimated to ±25% accuracy, with contingency of 15% of direct capital compared with the 2026 Scoping Study accuracy of ±30-50% with contingency of 30%
  • Long life domestic supply: mining and processing of 4.5 million tonnes per annum over 26 years, with average annual NdPr oxide production of approximately 2,500 tonnes, scheduled entirely from Probable Ore Reserves
  • Maiden Ore Reserve: Probable Ore Reserve of 116.4 million tonnes at 1,257 ppm payable rare earth oxide (PREO) declared at Cowboy State Mine
  • Feasibility Study advancing: drilling to convert Mineral Resources to Ore Reserves for the Feasibility Study is complete, with yttrium being assessed as a future product opportunity

DENVER, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- American Rare Earths Limited (ASX: ARR | OTCQX: ARRNF | ADR: AMRRY) (“ARR” or “the Company”) is pleased to announce the results of the Prefeasibility Study (“PFS”) for Cowboy State Mine (“CSM”), the first development phase of the Halleck Creek Project in Wyoming, together with the declaration of a maiden Probable Ore Reserve.

The PFS evaluates a 4.5 million tonne per annum open pit operation over 26 years, with estimated after tax NPV of approximately US$1.3B at an 8% real discount rate and pre-production capital of approximately US$840M, including contingency. It builds on the updated Scoping Study released on 30 September 2026,1 which brought forward PFS level mine planning and engineering to support the U.S. SEC Regulation S‑K, Subpart 1300 Initial Assessment prepared as part of the Company’s Nasdaq listing process. The Cowboy State Mine PFS contains less than 5% of the total Halleck Creek resource.

IMPORTANT DISCLOSURES

The PFS is a prefeasibility level technical and economic assessment, with capital and operating cost estimates prepared to a target accuracy of ±25%. The production target described in this announcement is based entirely on Probable Ore Reserves, which have been derived only from Indicated Mineral Resources. No Inferred Mineral Resources or Exploration Target material are scheduled as mill feed; Inferred material within the designed pits is treated as waste.

Recoveries downstream of the leach circuit are based on the Competent Person’s rare earth processing experience rather than completed test work and remain subject to confirmation through the pilot and demonstration program. There is no certainty that the production target or forecast financial outcomes will be realized. Further work, including a Feasibility Study, permitting and financing, is required before a development decision can be made.

Forecast outcomes depend on product prices, recoveries, capital and operating costs, technical performance, approvals and funding. This announcement contains forward-looking statements concerning development, test work, studies, partnerships and capital markets initiatives. Actual outcomes may differ materially because of technical, market, permitting, financing and operational risks.

“Declaring a maiden Ore Reserve is a defining step for Halleck Creek. It moves Cowboy State Mine from a resource with development potential to a defined mining project, supported by a prefeasibility level mine plan and cost estimate.

The PFS confirms the scale we outlined in the Scoping Study: 4.5 million tonnes a year over 26 years, producing around 2,500 tonnes of NdPr oxide annually. The cost estimates now carry a tighter accuracy range and a lower contingency, which gives investors and funding partners a firmer basis for assessing the project.

We also see clear room to improve on this base case. Our work with Novex is focused on lifting NdPr recovery and producing NdPr metal from Halleck Creek ore, and every percentage point of NdPr recovery is worth about US$50 million in project value. At the same time, we are working to reduce mining costs and improve how we manage waste streams.

We are advancing the underlying upstream Halleck Creek project while also working hard on our domestic mine to magnet supply chain. The work that is underway with Novex aims to see Halleck Creek ore taken through to oxide and NdPr metal using non-Chinese metal production methodology. The work continues for the largest US domestic rare earths deposit on a total contained rare earth basis.”

- Mark Wall, Chief Executive Officer, American Rare Earths

FROM RESOURCE TO RESERVE AT HALLECK CREEK

CSM is the first development phase of the broader Halleck Creek Project, which hosts a reported JORC Mineral Resource of approximately 2.63 billion tonnes at 3,292 ppm total rare earth oxides (“TREO”). Within this, the Indicated Mineral Resource for the CSM area is 391.4 million tonnes at 3,295 ppm TREO, estimated by Odessa Resources with an effective date of November 2025.

The PFS has converted part of that Indicated Mineral Resource into a maiden Probable Ore Reserve. The Ore Reserve represents approximately 30% of the CSM Indicated tonnage and is the first Ore Reserve declared for Halleck Creek. It establishes the reserve basis for the first phase of development while leaving substantial resource for later phases and for the Whole of Property Assessment.

Cowboy State Mine Ore Reserve, effective November 18, 2026

Notes: The Ore Reserve is reported above a payable rare earth oxide (PREO) cut-off grade of approximately 875 ppm, calculated as the sum of mining cost, process cost and general and administrative cost, divided by the product of the PREO price less royalty and the recovery. The pit optimization inputs were a mining cost of US$5.38 per tonne, a process cost of US$28.28 per tonne, general and administrative costs of US$1.10 per tonne and a Wyoming State royalty of 2.50%. Material above the cut-off is sent to the process plant and material below it reports to the waste rock storage facility or is used as construction material. The Mineral Resource is separately reported above a 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off derived from Stantec net smelter return calculations.

The Cowboy State Mine deposit will be mined by open-pit methods using conventional truck-and-shovel extraction; the mine plan does not include underground mining. Pit optimization was carried out in Whittle and the life-of-mine schedule was developed in Deswik. The mine plan moves 135.0 Mt of total material, comprising 116.4 Mt of ore and 18.7 Mt of waste at a strip ratio of 0.16:1, feeding the plant at 4.5 Mtpa over 26 years of production following a three-year construction period. Mining recovery is taken as 100% and mining dilution as nil, because the geological interpretation treats nearly all material within the pit as mineralized and the waste adjacent to the reserve is itself above cut-off grade Inferred material. Minimum mining widths are 32.5 m per bench and 28 m at the pit bottom, set by shovel swing radius, truck turning circle and safety berm requirements. Overall slope angles range from 54 degrees at a 300 m slope height to 45 degrees at 700 m, with a 50 degree inter-ramp angle applied in optimization; groundwater data was not available and was not incorporated in the geotechnical analysis. All ore in the schedule is drawn from the Indicated Mineral Resource; no Inferred material is scheduled as ore.

Run-of-mine ore is crushed to 100% passing 300 micron through a jaw crusher, cone crusher and vertical roller mill at the mine site, then concentrated approximately ten times using gravity separation in a reflux classifier concentrator together with dry induced roll magnetic separation and wet high intensity magnetic separation on the minus 50 micron fines stream. Concentrate is trucked to a refinery proposed at Wheatland, Wyoming, for dilute sulfuric acid tank leaching, impurity removal through two neutralization stages and uranium ion exchange, bulk solvent extraction, and solvent extraction separation and finishing into separate oxide products. Recoveries by unit operation are 78% through gravity and magnetic separation, 85% through leaching, 98% through partial neutralization and 96% through separation and finishing for NdPr oxide and 98% for the other products. The recoveries applied in the economic model are 58.2% for NdPr oxide, 25.8% for SEG oxide, 28.7% for terbium oxide and 12.4% for dysprosium oxide, giving an overall recovery of 49.9% of contained payable rare earth oxide. The process uses conventional unit operations, but yield losses downstream of the leach are based on the Competent Person’s rare earth processing experience rather than on completed test work, and the recoveries remain subject to confirmation by the pilot and demonstration plant program.

No statistical or geostatistical quantification of the relative accuracy of the Ore Reserve has been carried out. The estimate is global rather than local and carries the plus or minus 25% target accuracy of the underlying pre-feasibility level cost estimates. Confidence is supported by the conversion of Indicated Mineral Resources only, 100% mining recovery with nil dilution, and a mine plan returning a positive after-tax net present value in every single-variable downside case tested. Factors that may affect the estimate are unexpected variations in the quantity of mineralized material, grade or recovery, geotechnical conditions differing from those assumed, failure of plant, equipment or processes to operate as anticipated, and variations in project costs or metal prices. Groundwater data was not incorporated in the geotechnical analysis, no sustaining capital has been estimated for the processing and refinery facilities or site infrastructure over the 26-year mine life (mining fleet sustaining capital is included in the mining operating cost), and the metallurgical recoveries remain subject to pilot-scale confirmation. There are no production records against which to compare the estimate. A quantitative risk assessment is recommended at the feasibility stage.

PFS COMPARED WITH THE 2026 SCOPING STUDY

The 2026 Scoping Study already incorporated PFS level mine planning, which means the mine plan, throughput and modelled recoveries are largely unchanged. The PFS adds the Ore Reserve, a more definitive capital and operating cost estimate, and firmer infrastructure arrangements, including a signed water lease.

Discount rate, processing operating cost and processing capital cost are the next most significant variables.

MINING AND THE ORE RESERVE

CSM will be mined by conventional open pit truck and shovel methods. Stantec carried out pit optimization in Whittle and developed the life of mine schedule in Deswik. The mine plan moves 135.0 million tonnes of total material, comprising 116.4 million tonnes of ore and 18.7 million tonnes of waste, a strip ratio of 0.16:1, and feeds the plant at 4.5 million tonnes per annum over 26 years following a three-year construction period.

Mining recovery is taken as 100% and dilution as nil, because the geological interpretation treats nearly all material within the pit as mineralized and the material adjacent to the reserve is itself above cut off grade. Minimum mining widths of 32.5 m per bench and 28 m at the pit bottom were adopted, with overall slope angles ranging from 54 degrees at a 300 m slope height to 45 degrees at 700 m. Groundwater data was not available for the geotechnical analysis and will be incorporated in the Feasibility Study.

The final pit designs contain approximately 14% more waste than the selected optimization shell, reflecting design and operating constraints. The Ore Reserve is classified entirely as Probable because no Measured Mineral Resource has been reported.

The Probable classification follows from conversion of Indicated Mineral Resources after applying the PFS Modifying Factors, including pit optimization, a 10 m by 10 m by 10 m selective mining unit, the assumed 100% mining recovery and nil dilution, metallurgical recoveries, and infrastructure, cost and market assumptions. Ore Reserve confidence has been assessed qualitatively on a global basis rather than quantified statistically. Cost estimates target ±25% accuracy, while groundwater has not been incorporated in the pit slope analysis, downstream recoveries require pilot confirmation, processing and refinery sustaining capital beyond the planned waste disposal expansion has not been estimated, and permitting remains outstanding.

The Ore Reserve cut-off of approximately 875 ppm payable rare earth oxide (PREO) was calculated by comparing the recoverable value of the payable oxide products, net of royalty, with pit optimization inputs of US$5.38 per tonne for mining, US$28.28 per tonne for processing and US$1.10 per tonne for general and administrative costs. Material above this cut-off is processed; material below it is treated as waste or used for construction. This is distinct from the 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off used for reporting Mineral Resources.

PROCESSING FLOWSHEET AND RECOVERIES

Run of mine ore is crushed and ground to 100% passing 300 micron at the mine site using a jaw crusher, cone crusher and vertical roller mill. It is then concentrated approximately ten times through gravity separation in a reflux classifier, dry induced roll magnetic separation and wet high intensity magnetic separation of the fines. Concentrate is trucked to a refinery for dilute sulphuric acid tank leaching, two stage impurity removal, including disposal of deleterious elements (uranium and thorium), uranium ion exchange, bulk solvent extraction and separation into individual oxide products.

The recoveries applied in the PFS economic model are unchanged from the 2026 Scoping Study and give an overall recovery of 49.9% of contained payable rare earth oxide.

Iron and aluminium occur at levels requiring removal from the leach liquor, while uranium and thorium are present at low levels but require control for product quality and residue management. Zirconium, uranium, thorium and iron were estimated alongside rare earth grades in the Resource model. The PFS allows for staged neutralization and filtration to remove iron, thorium and aluminium, followed by uranium ion exchange; associated reagents, processing and waste disposal costs, including refinery waste facility expansion and closure, are included in the economic assumptions. No separate value is assigned to these impurities and no third-party treatment or product specification penalties are modelled for the oxide products sold FOB. Impurity deportment and residue characteristics remain subject to further testing and permitting.

To manage the seasonal availability of the contracted water supply, a water-supply pond with an indicative capacity of approximately 550 acre-feet is currently included in the capital costs.

CAPITAL AND OPERATING COSTS

Pre-production capital is estimated at US$840M, comprising direct capital of US$730M and a 15% contingency of US$110M. Of this, US$840M is spent over the three-year construction period, and a further US$33M of expansion capital is provided for staged development of the refinery waste disposal facility in 2034 and 2044, giving total life of Project capital of US$873M.

Closure costs of US$55.9 million, comprising US$30.9 million for mine closure and US$25.0 million for refinery waste disposal closure, are included in operating costs in the final year of the mine plan. Life of Project operating cost is estimated at US$4,726M undiscounted, equivalent to US$40.62 per tonne of ROM ore processed.

Sustaining capital for the replacement of the mining fleet is included in the mining unit rate. Sustaining capital was also included for the staged refinery waste disposal expansion and has been estimated. The Project is subject to a sliding scale Wyoming State royalty of 5% to 10%, a 2% Wyoming severance tax, a 7% Albany County ad valorem tax and a 0.875% industrial property tax. Total royalties, levies and federal income tax are estimated at US$1,785M over the life of the Project.

No offtake agreements are currently in place.

FUTURE OPPORTUNITY: YTTRIUM

Yttrium is present throughout the Halleck Creek Mineral Resource and is the largest single component of the heavy rare earth group, making up on average approximately 5.4% of TREO. It is not included in the PFS base case, Ore Reserve, production target or financial evaluation.

A mixed rare earth oxide produced from Halleck Creek ore in December 2025 confirmed yttrium is present in the product, although the flowsheet has not been optimized for yttrium. Early mineralogy indicates that a significant share of the yttrium may be hosted in minerals other than allanite, so the current test work is examining recovery routes both within and beyond the base case flowsheet. ARR is investigating yttrium recovery with U.S. Government research partners.

The program will confirm the minerals that host yttrium, test leach and separation conditions, develop a route to a commercial grade yttrium oxide product and define product specifications and market requirements. If this work demonstrates a viable recovery route and a supportable market, yttrium will be assessed for inclusion as a product in the Feasibility Study.

ADVANCING TO THE FEASIBILITY STUDY

Drilling to support the conversion of Mineral Resources to Ore Reserves for the Feasibility Study has been completed. Results from this program were not incorporated in the PFS and will be included in an updated Mineral Resource estimate to support the Feasibility Study. The PFS sets out a work program toward the Feasibility Study with an order of magnitude budget of approximately US$10 million.

Previously Reported Quality-of-Life Findings

Hemostemix reported results from 30 patients with paired SF-36 assessments at three and six months in its Phase I ischemic cardiomyopathy study defined the significant improvement in quality of life experienced by clinical trial study subjects.   • Exercise capacity: In a Phase I angina study, mean six-minute walk distance increased by 81.3 metres at three months and 79.6 metres at six months versus baseline, both p<0.001.

  • Cardiac function: In a severe-cardiomyopathy subgroup within a retrospective study, mean left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 14.6% to 28.4% at final follow-up-an improvement of 13.8 percentage points, equivalent to approximately 94.5% relative to the initial value.

These findings arose from different populations and study designs. However, they are indicative of clinically relevant statistically significant outcomes experienced by end stage no option heart patients.

A Clinical Foundation for Longevity Research

Hemostemix's proposed longevity program will investigate whether VesCell can improve measures relevant to healthspan, including improved physical capacity, cardiovascular function, cognition and immune system function (reduced inflammatory biomarkers). The Company announced Dr. Ernst von Schwarz as Principal Investigator.

"For patients, quality of life means having the energy and physical ability to remain active, independent and engaged in everyday life," said Thomas Smeenk, President and CEO. Our commercial success in this area will be fully supported by commercial clinical trials in The Bahamas at Doctors Hospital, " Smeenk said.

A VesCell Treated Heart: Improved cardiac function from remodelling and increased contractility 

Remodelling means a change in the heart's size and shape. A badly weakened left ventricle can enlarge and retain a great deal of blood after each beat. Here, both its full volume and estimated leftover volume fell. Together with the higher ejection fraction, that pattern is consistent with favourable reverse remodelling. Contractility means the heart muscle's intrinsic ability to generate force. Expelling roughly 54 mL from a smaller chamber, versus 39 mL from a larger one, shows better pumping performance and is compatible with improved contraction.

Three months later, it held 268 mL but expelled roughly 54 mL per heart beat (268 × 20%). Ejection fraction improved from 13.2% to 20%, a relative 51% improvement. MRI imaging showed reduced scaring, and increased viable heart muscle performance.

Hemostemix is an autologous stem cell therapy platform company, founded in 2003. A winner of the World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer Award, the Company has developed, patented, and is commercializing VesCell™ an investigational autologous stem cell therapy. Hemostemix has completed seven clinical studies of 318 subjects and published its results in eleven peer reviewed publications. ACP-01 is safe, and appears clinically relevant as a treatment for peripheral arterial disease, chronic limb threatening ischemia, non ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, ischemic cardiomyopathy, congestive heart failure, and angina. Hemostemix completed its Phase II clinical trial for chronic limb threatening ischemia and published its results in the Journal of Biomedical Research & Environmental Science. Innovative all-in-one marine communication solution earns top honors at Metstrade

OLATHE, Kan., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Garmin (NYSE: GRMN), the world's largest1 and most innovative marine electronics manufacturer, today announced the Garmin Signal™ VHF series was selected as an Overall Winner of the prestigious 2026 DAME Design Awards. The system also earned top honors in the Navigation & Communication category. Winners were announced at Metstrade, the world's largest exhibition of marine equipment, materials and systems, held Nov. 17-19 in Amsterdam.

This year's competition drew 153 entries, with 74 products nominated for the awards – the highest number of products shortlisted in over two decades. For the first time in the program's history, the jury of industry and design experts and media representatives selected three Overall Winners that represented excellence in every facet of product design across eight categories.

"We designed the Garmin Signal VHF series to rethink what boaters should expect from one of the most essential pieces of equipment at the helm. From its modern touchscreen design to integrated AIS and advanced communication capabilities, every detail makes the experience simpler and more intuitive. We're honored that the DAME jury recognized this new system with Garmin's first Overall DAME Design Award win." –Jarrod Seymour, Garmin Vice President and Marine Segment Leader

In one compact solution, Garmin Signal VHF delivers communication, situational awareness and intuitive operation. The radios feature an industry-first 3.5-inch color touchscreen with edge-to-edge glass, and the Signal VHF 400 adds an integrated Class B AIS transponder that helps boaters stay aware of surrounding vessel traffic. Boaters can transmit and receive VHF, DSC and AIS communications through a single VHF antenna, and can pair the system with the Signal RM 100 remote station to control the radio from a second helm or flybridge.

The jury noted: "The design of the new Garmin Signal range of VHF marine radios expands on all expected functions of a VHF and adds much more, including fully integrated AIS transmit and receive (using just one antenna), advanced channel monitoring capabilities and the ability to recall the last three minutes of a transmission. The radio and visually identical remote station appear to take their styling cues from Garmin's Fusion audio range with an aesthetic that will sit nicely within any modern helm station." 

The coveted DAME Design Award caps off another prolific year for Garmin Marine and follows other industry recognitions from the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA), IBEX, Soundings Trade Only, and the Sea Tow Foundation. DENVER, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- (247MarketNews)—While Americans get ready for Thanksgiving, Kraig Biocraft Laboratories (OTCQB: KBLB) has an international business date on the calendar. Chief Operating Officer Jon Rice is scheduled to present at the International Sericultural Commission Congress in Chennai, India, November 23–27, bringing Kraig’s recombinant spider-silk technology to an audience that knows how to produce, process and sell silk.

The congress runs Monday through Friday, spanning the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, November 26. Its theme, Silk For A Sustainable Future, gives Rice an industry setting for discussing what genetic engineering can add to one of the world’s oldest textile trades.

Kraig announced that Rice will address genetic engineering’s commercial impact on silk, including applications and production economics. The company sees the trip as an opportunity to strengthen industry relationships, explore complementary capabilities and pursue new markets.

“Silk is a material with a long history, and it is being reshaped for new applications and new markets,” Rice said.

Kraig’s production approach connects genetic engineering with sericulture, the cultivation of silkworms. Its engineered animals produce silk containing key spider-silk proteins, and their cocoons can be processed into yarn. The company has designed its platform to work within established silk-industry infrastructure.

Editor’s opinion: “There is a practical brilliance to bringing an advanced fiber into an industry that already knows how to raise silkworms and process cocoons. Kraig is giving an ancient craft a new material to work with. That makes the Silk Road connection especially fitting.”

Rice will have commercial progress to discuss. On September 29, Kraig announced shipment of its first commercial recombinant spider silk yarn order to a globally recognized performance sports brand. The yarn was processed to the customer’s specifications for a confidential pilot development program. That delivery gives the company an example of material made and shipped for a particular customer application.

The production operation also moved forward. In its October 5 update, Kraig reported all three production centers running on staggered schedules. The centers’ parental breeding lines supply hybrid eggs for subsequent cocoon production. The company also reported that its last production run had increased silk output by more than 30% through the rainy season.

On October 26, Kraig announced a program to develop additional yarn constructions and blends, alongside a requested sample shipment to a textile innovator with experience collaborating with major aerospace manufacturers. That work puts the focus on how the fiber can be prepared for different uses, with yarn development providing a connection between the material and the manufacturer.

The company’s stated interest in complementary capabilities gives the trip a practical purpose. Experienced silk producers and processors bring knowledge of rearing, reeling and textile manufacturing. Those are the same kinds of capabilities involved in turning cocoons into yarn that a customer can evaluate.

Editor’s opinion: “We like seeing Jon Rice working hard for shareholders during Thanksgiving week. Kraig has made its first commercial shipment; now it needs to put that material in front of the people who can help develop its next applications and expand its reach. New Patent Strengthens Cingulate’s Intellectual Property Portfolio While Company Maintains Focus on Advancing Lead ADHD Candidate CTx-1301

KANSAS CITY, Kan., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING), a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) drug delivery platform to develop a pipeline of next-generation pharmaceutical products, today announced that the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has issued U.S. Patent No. 12,797,335, titled "Trimodal, Precision-Timed Release Tablet."

The newly issued patent covers a buspirone tablet formulation incorporating Cingulate's proprietary PTR™ technology, which is designed to release medication at three separate, predetermined times throughout the day from a single tablet. Buspirone is an FDA-approved treatment for anxiety disorders. The patented formulation supports the Company's development of CTx-2103 and further demonstrates the versatility and broader applicability of Cingulate's technology beyond its initial focus on ADHD.

"Cingulate remains focused on advancing CTx-1301, our lead ADHD treatment candidate, toward NDA resubmission and commercialization in the second half of 2027, if approved. We believe CTx-2103 represents an attractive opportunity to build a pipeline of assets beyond ADHD with our proprietary PTR™ Platform. The issuance of this patent further strengthens the Company’s intellectual property portfolio. Following approval of CTx-1301, Cingulate anticipates initiating the development of CTx-2103," said Cingulate Chairman and CEO Shane J. Schaffer.

About U.S. Patent No. 12,797,335

U.S. Patent No. 12,797,335, titled "Trimodal, Precision-Timed Release Tablet," was issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office on November 17, 2026. The patent covers a pharmaceutical tablet formulation designed to deliver three separate releases of an active pharmaceutical ingredient at predetermined intervals following administration. The patented technology utilizes Cingulate's proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) approach to control the timing of medication release from a single oral dosage form. The patent covers a buspirone formulation relevant to Cingulate's investigational CTx-2103 candidate for the treatment of anxiety disorders and further expands the Company's intellectual property portfolio surrounding its proprietary drug delivery technology.

About Anxiety

Anxiety disorders are the most common category of mental disorders in the United States, affecting nearly 30 percent of adults at some point during their lives, according to the American Psychiatric Association.¹ Anxiety is a normal response to stress or perceived danger and can help individuals prepare for challenging situations. However, when excessive anxiety becomes persistent, difficult to control, and interferes with everyday activities, it may constitute an anxiety disorder.² According to the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), an estimated 31.1 percent of U.S. adults experience an anxiety disorder at some point during their lives.³ Despite the availability of effective treatments, anxiety disorders frequently go undiagnosed or untreated, with research indicating that delays between the onset of symptoms and initial treatment can extend for many years.⁴ The COVID-19 pandemic further highlighted the growing burden of mental health conditions, with the World Health Organization reporting a 25 percent increase in the global prevalence of anxiety and depression during the first year of the pandemic.⁵

About CTx-2103

CTx-2103 utilizes a novel multi-core formulation of buspirone, an FDA-approved treatment for anxiety.

CTx-2103 will be designed as a once-daily, modified-release tablet with clear differentiation and compelling advantages over standard treatment options which must be taken multiple times per day to maximize efficacy.

Cingulate completed a proof-of-concept study in which pharmacokinetics were evaluated for a trimodal tablet providing three precisely timed doses of buspirone. In addition, scintigraphic imaging visualized transit of the tablet through the gastrointestinal tract to confirm both the site and onset of release, which was then correlated with pharmacokinetic data to establish the full release profile of the CTx-2103 formulation. Based on the pharmacokinetic profile seen in the data, CTx-2103 achieved a triple release of buspirone. These results provided the critical information required to complete a Pre-IND meeting with FDA to discuss the design of the clinical and regulatory program.

About Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

ADHD is a chronic neurobiological and developmental disorder that affects millions of children and often continues into adulthood. The estimated market size of the US ADHD market is approximately 100 million annual prescriptions. The condition is marked by an ongoing pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development. In the U.S., over 20 million patients have been diagnosed with ADHD. Among this group, 12 million are adults and over 8 million are under the age of 17. According to the CDC, just 53.6 percent of all children and teens with ADHD reported they were actively treating their symptoms with medication in 2022, with 65-90 percent demonstrating clinical ADHD symptoms that persist into adulthood. Current market trends demonstrate that adult ADHD prevalence is larger and growing faster than the child and adolescent segments combined.

About CTx-1301

CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) is a once-daily, multi-core tablet utilizing Cingulate’s proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) platform to deliver three precisely timed releases of active medication across the day. This design aims to provide rapid onset of effect and entire active-day duration. CTx-1301 is being evaluated for the treatment of ADHD under the FDA’s 505(b)(2) pathway. In October 2025, the FDA accepted for review the NDA for CTx-1301 and assigned a PDUFA target action date of May 31, 2026. On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for the CTx-1301 NDA; the Company and its CDMO have since substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests, and the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2026. There can be no assurance regarding the timing of any resubmission or whether approval will occur.

About Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) Platform Technology

Cingulate is developing ADHD and anxiety disorder product candidates capable of achieving true once-daily dosing using Cingulate’s innovative PTR drug delivery platform technology. It incorporates a proprietary Erosion Barrier Layer (EBL) providing control of drug release at precise, pre-defined times with no release of drug prior to the intended release. The EBL technology is enrobed around a drug-containing core to give a tablet-in-tablet dose form. It is designed to erode at a controlled rate until eventually the drug is released from the core tablet. The EBL formulation, Oralogik™, is licensed from BDD Pharma. Cingulate intends to utilize its PTR technology to expand and augment its clinical-stage pipeline by identifying and developing additional product candidates in other therapeutic areas in addition to Anxiety and ADHD.

About Cingulate Inc.

Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING) is a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary PTR drug delivery platform technology to build and advance a pipeline of next-generation pharmaceutical products, designed to improve the lives of patients suffering from frequently diagnosed conditions characterized by burdensome daily dosing regimens and suboptimal treatment outcomes. With an initial focus on the treatment of ADHD, Cingulate is identifying and evaluating additional therapeutic areas where PTR technology may be employed to develop future product candidates, including to treat anxiety disorders. Cingulate is headquartered in Kansas City. For more information, visit Cingulate.com.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Heineken® has revealed Czech F1 fan Lukáš Chalabala as the winner of the Heineken® x F1® Season Ticket - a limited edition 1/1 - securing him access to every single race on the 2027 calendar.

Throughout the season, Lukáš will get the chance to travel the world and connect with the sport’s passionate fan community at every single stop, experiencing the best of F1. He and a guest will have access to the best grandstand seats, travel and accommodation covered worldwide by Heineken®.

Lukáš - who had never before experienced the thrill of F1 racing in person - was handed the one-of-a-kind carbon fibre pass by Brandon Burgess, the inaugural Heineken® x F1® Season Ticket holder at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. In a full-circle moment, the pair were surprised by four-time F1® world champion and Heineken® 0.0 ambassador Max Verstappen who presented Brandon with the inaugural ticket back in 2025.

The search for the 2027 Heineken® x F1® Season Ticket holder began in July, and attracted hundreds of thousands of fans. After reaching the final, along with five others from the UK, US, New Zealand and Singapore, Lukáš won the fan vote - hosted on F1® Unlocked.

Lukáš Chalabala, 2027 Heineken® x F1® Season Ticket holder says, “I’ve been a fan of F1 for as long as I can remember, but I’ve never had the chance to experience a race in person, so to win something like this is a dream come true. I said in my submission video that winning the Season Ticket would finally give my sofa some peace, so hopefully I won’t be using it too much next year! I’m most looking forward to experiencing every single race weekend up close and meeting fellow F1 fans from all over the world along the way. Twenty-four races, different cultures and countless unforgettable moments - I still can’t quite believe it’s actually happening! Knowing how many fans voted for me online feels surreal, and I want to make sure I give something back by taking them along on this incredible journey and sharing as much of the experience as I can.”

Brandon Burgess, 2026 Heineken® x F1® Season Ticket holder says, “I’ve had such an incredible year with this ticket, so I’m beyond excited to pass the experience onto another huge F1® fan. Having met so many great people and having made countless memories, all of which I'll remember for the rest of my life, I know that Lukáš has got a lot to look forward to, and I’m already excited to follow his journey with the ticket-of-a-lifetime next year!”

Four-time world champion and Heineken® 0.0 Ambassador, Max Verstappen says, “The Heineken® x F1® Season Ticket is the coolest opportunity I’ve seen for an F1 fan. Having the chance to experience every Grand Prix across the season is incredibly rare, and Lukáš will get to see so much more than just the racing. Being at every race will give him a unique insight into the sport, understanding the details and decisions that go into a race weekend whilst meeting new people along the way. He’ll also get to explore the cities and experience the culture of each place, which is something I don’t always get the chance to do myself when travelling from race to race. MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--SentinelOne® (NYSE: S), the AI Security leader, today announced it will partner with the Defence Cyber Command (DCCOM) of the Digital and Intelligence (DIS) to collaboratively strengthen cyber defence and advance secure AI across Singapore’s defence and critical infrastructure sectors. The relationship was formalised at CIDEX 2026.

The rapid adoption of AI has fundamentally changed cybersecurity norms and best practices. In the few months alone, the emergence and exploitation of novel vulnerabilities, rogue AI agent behavior, and LLM-related supply chain attacks, have ushered in a new era in cyber governance and defence.

SentinelOne and DCCOM will explore bringing together the AI-native Singularity™ Platform, SentinelLABS™ AI and threat intelligence research, and training with DCCOM’s own expertise to help defenders evolve their practices and strategies to meet this new reality. As a result, human defenders can benefit from AI-powered security to detect, investigate, and respond to novel threats at machine speed.

Security That Fits Defence Environments

Defence networks need protection that does not depend on a cloud connection. The Singularity Platform supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment, so DCCOM can apply AI-native protection in environments where a cloud connection is not an option. For defenders, that means detection and response that stay inside the network boundary.

Four Areas of Cooperation

The parties will explore partnering in four areas:

- Cybersecurity technology and solutions
- Cyber threat intelligence sharing
- Research and innovation
- Training and capacity building

“Singapore is putting AI at the centre of how it defends itself and runs its critical systems, and the security behind that has to keep pace,” said Andrew Howell, VP, Government Affairs at SentinelOne. “This collaboration allows us to explore ways our platform, our research, and our training can be combined alongside DCCOM's own teams, so defenders can stop attacks at machine speed, including in air-gapped environments, and so more of the people doing that work are trained in Singapore.”

“Our MOU with SentinelOne will facilitate joint collaboration on AI-enabled technologies for cyber operations, for faster threat detection, investigation and response at machine speed,” said Brigadier-General Clarence Cai, Commander DCCOM/Defence Cyber Chief.

SentinelOne (NYSE: S) is the leader in AI security, setting the standard for using AI and automation to give defenders a decisive operating advantage. Key Terms

air-gappedtechnical
A system described as air-gapped is physically isolated from public and private networks so it cannot be reached over the internet or company LAN, like a safe kept in a room with no phone line. For investors this matters because air-gapping reduces the risk that critical data, trading algorithms, backups or industrial controls will be accessed or tampered with by hackers, but it can also increase costs and slow information flow compared with connected systems.
llmtechnical
A large language model (LLM) is an advanced computer system trained on vast amounts of written text to understand and generate human-like language, similar to a very fast, well-read assistant that can summarize documents, draft messages, or answer questions. Investors care because LLMs can speed up research, automate customer support, and reduce costs, while also creating new product opportunities and risks around accuracy, bias, and regulatory oversight that can affect a company’s performance.

MESA, AZ / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Medical Care Technologies Inc. (OTCID:MDCE) today announced that it has paused dilution and does not currently plan to resume equity issuance until 2027 when expansion plans and funding are to be re-evaluated in efforts to align with shareholder value and continuing near term revenue. The decision follows the Company's third-quarter results showing a sharp improvement in profitability and accelerating private sales activity at its Infinite Auctions subsidiary.

On November 12, MDCE reported unaudited results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third-quarter sales revenue rose 13% to $538,981. Gross profit increased 55% to $240,839. Net operating income rose 254% to $192,565, and net income increased 270% to $192,565. For the nine-month period, the Company reported net income of $198,883 compared to a net loss of $145,347 in the prior-year period. Gross profit rose to $332,744. The Company ended the quarter with zero current liabilities and cash of $102,172.

Supporting the decision to pause dilution is revenue generation at Infinite Auctions. Private sales at the subsidiary have already surpassed $300,000 in the fourth quarter. This activity builds on the subsidiary's partnership with a multi-billion-dollar sports card and collectibles company, under which six-figure transaction activity has already occurred. Real Game Used continues to maintain a continuous backlog of customer and auction-brand authentication work through its automated submission system. The Company has also announced that its subsidiaries are managing approximately $20 million in private collectibles assets, with potential net profits contingent on completed sales.

In parallel, technical development continues under MDCE's first paid external software agreement, valued at up to $250,000, covering an integrated web and enterprise platform for inventory and sales workflows. The first payment under that agreement has been initiated. StrainScan Pro enterprise demonstrations remain active. Internal evaluation continues on MDCE Melanoma Scan Beta and the wound-monitoring application, with updated technical results available on the Company's corporate website.

"Shareholders have expressed concern about dilution and this is our response," said Marshall Perkins, CEO of Medical Care Technologies. "The third-quarter results showed net income up 270% and a clear improvement in profitability. Infinite Auctions private sales have already surpassed $300,000 in Q4. That revenue, together with the software agreement now in active development and the ongoing work at our subsidiaries, gives us the ability to pause further equity issuance through 2027. The focus is on building from the commercial activity we already have in motion."

Delivery of an ADS-TEC Energy BESS5000 battery storage system to German municipal utility Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg-Kornwestheim (SWLB). Following its successful commissioning, SWLB has ordered two additional systems with a combined capacity of 10 MWh

  • Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg-Kornwestheim (SWLB) places repeat order for two additional ADS-TEC Energy battery storage systems with a combined capacity of 10 megawatt-hours
  • The new systems will increase flexibility in the local power grid and support the development of a resilient, decentralized energy infrastructure
  • Battery storage technology developed and integrated in Germany

NÜRTINGEN, Germany & LUDWIGSBURG, Germany--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- ADS-TEC Energy has secured a repeat order from German municipal utility Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg-Kornwestheim (SWLB) for two additional battery energy storage systems. The two BESS5000 systems have a combined capacity of 10 megawatt-hours and will be installed at the Reuteallee site in Ludwigsburg. Commissioning is scheduled for summer 2027.

Delivery of an ADS-TEC Energy BESS5000 battery storage system.

Only about a year ago, SWLB placed an order with ADS-TEC Energy for a 5-megawatt-hour battery storage system, which is now operational at the utility's wood-fired combined heat and power plant in Ludwigsburg. The new order builds on the successful collaboration between the two companies.

German Battery Storage Technology for Municipal Energy Infrastructure

SWLB is pursuing a decentralized energy storage strategy, deploying multiple battery storage systems across its service area. The systems are designed to facilitate the integration of renewable energy, reduce strain on the power grid and create additional opportunities to participate in energy markets.

ADS-TEC Energy develops its battery storage technology in Germany and integrates the key technical components into a precisely matched overall system.

Michael Rudloff, COO of ADS-TEC Energy, comments: "We are pleased that SWLB has once again placed its trust in us and that we are continuing our successful collaboration. When building a decentralized energy storage infrastructure, it is essential that individual systems operate reliably and integrate seamlessly into existing systems. This is where we contribute our many years of experience in developing and integrating battery storage systems. The project shows that, in this area of critical infrastructure, local partnerships lead to effective solutions."

Sebastian Hess, Strategy and Corporate Development at Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg, adds: "The additional storage systems are a key component for a future-ready energy infrastructure and support the expansion of renewable energy in the region. By participating in the balancing market, we also aim to contribute to grid stability."

About ADS-TEC Energy

Building on more than 15 years of experience with lithium-ion technologies, ADS-TEC Energy develops and manufactures battery storage solutions and fast-charging systems, including their energy management systems.

Headquartered in Nürtingen, Germany, the company supports industrial companies, energy utilities and mobility providers in implementing modern energy solutions.
